new_entities.name: Gut microbiome diversity
new_entities.description: Diversity and richness of the gut microbial community.

edges.effect_quant: A 2025 soccer-player randomized trial found kefir increased Shannon and Chao1 diversity over 28 days, but a separate placebo-controlled ADHD trial found no significant overall alpha- or beta-diversity effect after six weeks. The broader dairy microbiome review also concluded diversity changes are inconsistent across kefir and related interventions.
edges.population: children or adults consuming kefir daily for several weeks in free-living or trial settings
edges.mechanism: Kefir supplies live microbes and fermentation products that can shift gut community structure, but effects appear context-dependent and may influence specific taxa more consistently than broad diversity metrics.
edges.summary: Kefir is better framed as microbiome-mixed than as a guaranteed diversity booster. Some trials show richer microbial profiles, but others find little change in alpha diversity despite shifts in individual taxa and symptoms.
edges.caveats: The evidence base is still small and population-specific. Positive findings in athletes or symptomatic children should not be generalized into a universal claim that kefir reliably increases diversity in everyone.
